- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) — reduce initial forecast by 1–2%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) — add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for risk aversion.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price drops — cap forecast increases at 3% above prior day unless sentiment >0.7.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3-day average of forecast is >10% above true, adjust downward by 1–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overconfidence in “trending” signals — if sentiment is neutral or declining, reduce forecast slope by 20–30%.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
